c.st: Effective altruism is not effective
c.x:
If you're not convinced by this article, or simply want to know more about effective altruism, a good place to start is Peter Singer's free book The Life You Can Save, available at https://www.thelifeyoucansave.org/the-book/. (You can use a fake email if you don't want to give your real one).

I highly recommend it. The concepts of EA have been life changing for me, permanently changing my perspective on the how to live a good life. I'm happier and more purposeful as a result.

c.st: Did James Damore really deserve to be fired for what he wrote? (P. Singer)

He's one of the world's most pre-eminent bioethicists.

His writings on animal welfare (e.g., The Way We Eat) and fighting poverty (e.g., The Expanding Circle, The Life You Can Save) are fantastic and should be required reading.

c.st: The ‘effective altruists’
c.x:
I've read this book together with the two books about Effective Altruism bei Peter Singer (The Life You Can Save and The Most Good You Can Do), and I have to say these books have really changed my life. I know it sounds cheesy, but I've never read books that had such a lasting influence on me.

Those books provide just the right rational and scientific arguments and have shown me with how much cognitive dissonance I, as a supposed rational person, ran through my life.

c.st: Forgotten Woodlands
c.x:
Sherwood is not forgotten of course. Every fan of Robin Hood knows it. But it had the misfortune to be in an early industrial area.

I mentioned Birnam Wood in another post, which features in MacBeth. Shakespeare plays fast and loose with Scottish history, but Birnam Wood was a real place. One or two of the old trees are still there, but not much. The area has been reforested a bit within the past two hundred years.
